newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rebels strike again, hand over bodies.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rebels strike again, hand over bodies.

text.p: Tamil rebels raided the Sri Lankan military's defences in the north on Sunday, three days after a major attack on a northern army base in which at least 142 soldiers were killed, military officials said.

The rebels made a pre-dawn raid on the army's forward defences at Chettikulam in the Vavuniya district, 240 km (150 miles) north of the capital Colombo, killing at least five soldiers, military officials in the area said.
An official at the Ministry of Defence in Colombo confirmed that the raid took place, but said details were not available.

Later on Sunday the rebels offered to hand over what they said were the bodies of 27 soldiers killed in last week's rebel assault on Paranthan, a key road-junction town 280 km (185 miles) north of Colombo, to the Red Cross, Sivanathan Kishore of the Sri Lanka Red Cross told Reuters.
Military officials in Vavuniya refused to accept the bodies saying they were difficult to identify, Kishore said.
"I have sent the bodies back to the other (rebel) side for cremation," Kishore said.

The Defence Ministry said on Saturday that 350 Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) guerrillas and 161 soldiers were killed in Thursday's attack on the Paranthan base, the first military base to come under attack this year by the rebels in the fiercest fighting since last September.
The LTTE said it had lost 140 fighters, including 78 women, in the attack.
Up to 700 rebels and more than 200 soldiers were wounded in the Paranthan battle, the Defence Ministry said.
The LTTE, fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in this predominantly Sinhalese island nation, called Thursday's attack a success.

"Strategically, the LTTE's twin objective of dispersing troop concentrations and nullifying Sri Lanka's fire power by setting fire to ammunition dumps and destroying its heavy guns, proved an overwhelming success," a statement issued from the rebels' London office said on Sunday.
"The LTTE victories at Paranthan gave a strong message to the Sri Lankan government not to persist with its military solution to the Tamil national question," the statement said.

The government of President Chandrika Kumaratunga has been following a two-pronged strategy of militarily weakening the Tigers in the bid to force the rebels to talks, while offering autonomy to woo ethnic Tamils away from the rebels' demand for independence, political analysists said.

Last week's attack, which forced army gunners to destroy several artillery pieces to prevent them from falling into rebel hands, shows guerrilla chief Velupillai Prabhakaran retains his formidable military machine, the analysts said.

The rebels said the attack was a costly one for the military. Their statement said 11 large artillery pieces, the camp's fleet of armoured vehicles and a 10 km (six miles) stretch of bunkers and sentry points were destroyed.
"It is estimated that many millions of rupees worth of military equipment was wiped away in a short space of time," the LTTE said.
But the army said its soldiers destroyed the artillery pieces and ammunition dump themselves to prevent them from falling into rebel hands.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the 14-year conflict. The LTTE says the toll is much higher.
